results.title: Extensions of prime degree with a nontrivial automorphism are Galois
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In an extension of prime degree, a nontrivial automorphism witnesses that the extension is Galois, has order equal to the degree, and generates the automorphism group.

results.title: Intermediate fields of an abelian extension form a modular lattice

results.title: Norm in a tensor product with a Galois extension
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a Galois extension `M / F` and any `F`-algebra `R`, the norm of an element of `R ⊗[F] M` over `R` is the product of its Galois conjugates.

results.title: The closure of a Galois subgroup is the fixing group of its fixed field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K/k$ be a Galois extension, not necessarily finite, and give $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ the Krull topology. For every subgroup $H$ of $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ with fixed field $K^H$, the closure of $H$ equals the subgroup of $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ consisting of the automorphisms that fix $K^H$ pointwise.

results.title: Fibonacci prime divisibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p > 2$ and $p \ne 5$, and let $\left(\frac{5}{p}\right)$ be the Legendre symbol of $5$ modulo $p$. Then $p$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_{p-1}$ if $\left(\frac{5}{p}\right) = 1$, and $p$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_{p+1}$ otherwise. Since $\left(\frac{5}{p}\right) = \pm 1$, this says that $p$ divides $F_{p - \left(\frac{5}{p}\right)}$.

results.title: The $5$-adic valuation of Fibonacci numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Writing $F_n$ for the $n$-th Fibonacci number and $v_5$ for the $5$-adic valuation, $v_5(F_n) = v_5(n)$ for every integer $n \ge 1$.

results.title: Normalized Ihara ratio
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $g \in \mathbb{N}$, the normalized ratio of $N$ at $g$ is the extended nonnegative real $N(g)/g$ when $g > 0$, and $0$ when $g = 0$.

results.title: Abstract Ihara constant of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is $\limsup_{g \to \infty} N(g)/g \in [0, \infty]$, the limit superior as $g \to \infty$ of the normalized ratios of $N$.

results.title: Eventual ratio bounds bound the abstract Ihara constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c \in [0, \infty]$. If the normalized ratio of $N$ at $g$ is at most $c$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is at most $c$.

results.title: Lower bound for the Ihara constant from the normalized ratios
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $c \in [0, \infty]$, and for each $g \in \mathbb{N}$ let $r_N(g) \in [0, \infty]$ be the normalized ratio $N(g)/g$, with $r_N(0) = 0$. If $c \le r_N(g)$ for infinitely many $g$, then $c \le \limsup_{g \to \infty} r_N(g)$, the Ihara constant of $N$.

results.title: Linear upper bound on a normalized ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $g \in \mathbb{N}$ and $c \in [0, \infty]$. If $N(g) \le c \cdot g$ in $[0, \infty]$, then the normalized ratio of $N$ at $g$ is at most $c$.

results.title: Lower bound for one normalized Ihara ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $c \in [0, \infty]$ and $g > 0$ an integer. If $c \cdot g \le N(g)$ in $[0, \infty]$, then $c \le N(g)/g$, where the normalized ratio $N(g)/g$ is taken in $[0, \infty]$.

results.title: Eventual linear upper bound on the abstract Ihara constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c \in [0, \infty]$. If $N(g) \le c \cdot g$ in $[0, \infty]$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is at most $c$.

results.title: Eventual affine upper bound on the abstract Ihara constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $c \in [0, \infty]$ and $d \in [0, \infty)$. If $N(g) \le c \cdot g + d$ in $[0, \infty]$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is at most $c$.

results.title: Lower bound for the Ihara constant from a linear bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c \in [0, \infty]$. If there are infinitely many integers $g > 0$ with $c \cdot g \le N(g)$ in $[0, \infty]$, then $c \le \limsup_{g \to \infty} N(g)/g$, the Ihara constant of $N$, where the ratio $N(g)/g$ is taken in $[0, \infty]$ and set to $0$ at $g = 0$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the normalized ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N, M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $g \in \mathbb{N}$. If $N(g) \le M(g)$, then the normalized ratio of $N$ at $g$ is at most the normalized ratio of $M$ at $g$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the abstract Ihara constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N, M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If $N(g) \le M(g)$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is at most that of $M$.

results.title: The abstract Ihara constant ignores finitely many values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N, M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If $N(g) = M(g)$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then $N$ and $M$ have the same abstract Ihara constant. In particular, changing finitely many values of $N$ does not change its abstract Ihara constant.

results.title: Agreement from an index onward preserves the abstract Ihara constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N, M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $G \in \mathbb{N}$. If $N(g) = M(g)$ for every $g \ge G$, then $N$ and $M$ have the same abstract Ihara constant.

part.title: Alternating sign matrices and Robbins numbers

path: Alternating sign matrices and Robbins numbers

results.title: Robbins numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Robbins number $A_n$ is the natural number obtained by dividing $\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} (3k+1)!$ by $\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} (n+k)!$, where the division is division of natural numbers rounded down.

results.title: Signed Robbins numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the signed Robbins number is the integer $(-1)^{\binom{n+1}{2}} A_{n+1}$, where $A_{n+1}$ is the Robbins number.

results.title: Row partial sums of a matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an $n \times n$ integer matrix $A$ and indices $i, k \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the row partial sum of $A$ at $(i, k)$ is the sum of the entries of row $i$ in columns $0$ through $k$, that is, $\sum_{j \le k} A_{ij}$.

results.title: Column partial sums of a matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an $n \times n$ integer matrix $A$ and indices $j, k \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the column partial sum of $A$ at $(j, k)$ is the sum of the entries of column $j$ in rows $0$ through $k$, that is, $\sum_{i \le k} A_{ij}$.

results.title: Integers equal to zero or one
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integer $a$ is zero or one when $a = 0$ or $a = 1$. These are the values allowed for the partial sums of an alternating sign matrix.

results.title: Alternating sign matrices
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An $n \times n$ integer matrix $A$ is an alternating sign matrix when every entry of $A$ is $-1$, $0$ or $1$; for all indices $i, k$ the row partial sum $\sum_{j \le k} A_{ij}$ is $0$ or $1$; for all indices $j, k$ the column partial sum $\sum_{i \le k} A_{ij}$ is $0$ or $1$; every row of $A$ sums to $1$; and every column of $A$ sums to $1$.

results.title: Alternating sign matrices of size $n$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the collection of all $n \times n$ integer matrices that are alternating sign matrices.

results.title: The Robbins product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Robbins product is the rational number

results.title: Alternating sign matrix theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the number of $n \times n$ alternating sign matrices equals the Robbins product $\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} \frac{(3k+1)!}{(n+k)!}$.

results.title: Generalized Kullback–Leibler divergence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Kullback–Leibler `β = 1` divergence `d(x | y) = x log (x / y) - x + y` (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 4). With Mathlib's `0 * log _ = 0` it gives `d(0 | y) = y`, the correct value; `y > 0` is needed when `x > 0`.

results.title: Reconstruction matrix in nonnegative matrix factorization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The reconstruction `(W H)_fn = ∑_k w_fk h_kn`.

results.title: Data-fit term of the ARD-NMF objective
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The data-fit term `D_1(V | W H) = ∑_{f,n} d(v_fn | (W H)_fn)`.

results.title: H-dependent part of the ARD-NMF objective
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `H`-dependent part `D_1(V | W H) / φ + ∑_{k,n} h_kn / λ_k` of the `ℓ₁`-ARD objective (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 20, `β = 1`).

results.title: ARD multiplicative update of H
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `ℓ₁`-ARD multiplicative update of `H` for `β = 1` (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 32, Algorithm 2): `h_kn ← h_kn (∑_f w_fk v_fn / (W H)_fn) / (∑_f w_fk + φ / λ_k)`.

results.title: The `H` update is monotone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `H` update is monotone (Tan–Févotte 2013, §IV-B, `β = 1`): it does not increase `D_1(V | W H) / φ + ∑ h_kn / λ_k`, for `φ > 0`, `λ > 0`, `V ≥ 0`, `W ≥ 0` with no zero row, and `H > 0` entrywise.

results.title: W-dependent part of the ARD-NMF objective
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `W`-dependent part `D_1(V | W H) / φ + ∑_{f,k} w_fk / λ_k` of the `ℓ₁`-ARD objective (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 20, `β = 1`).

results.title: ARD multiplicative update of W
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `ℓ₁`-ARD multiplicative update of `W` for `β = 1` (Tan–Févotte, Algorithm 2): `w_fk ← w_fk (∑_n v_fn h_kn / (W H)_fn) / (∑_n h_kn + φ / λ_k)`.

results.title: The `W` update is monotone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It does not increase `D_1(V | W H) / φ + ∑ w_fk / λ_k`, for `φ > 0`, `λ > 0`, `V ≥ 0`, `H ≥ 0` with no zero column, and `W > 0` entrywise (the transpose of `objectiveH_updateH_le`).

results.title: Relevance update in ARD-NMF
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The relevance update `λ_k = (‖w_k‖₁ + ‖h_k‖₁ + b) / c` (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 33, `ℓ₁` prior; `c = F + N + a + 1`).

results.title: The relevance update is the exact minimizer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The relevance update is the exact minimizer (Tan–Févotte, §IV-C): for `A > 0` and `c > 0`, `λ ↦ A / λ + c log λ` attains its minimum over `λ > 0` at `λ = A / c`.

results.title: The minimizer is unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `λ > 0` does as well as `A / c`, then `λ = A / c`.

results.title: Lower bound on the relevance update
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The relevance never falls below its floor `b / c` (`W, H ≥ 0`, `c > 0`).

results.title: Pruning
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pruning (Tan–Févotte, §IV-D): the relevance equals its floor `b / c` exactly when the `k`-th column of `W` and the `k`-th row of `H` are zero (`W, H ≥ 0`, `c > 0`).

results.title: A pruned entry stays pruned
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The multiplicative update maps a zero entry of `H` to zero.

results.summary: The multiplicative update maps a zero entry of `W` to zero.
